name: io.github.codytodd-ui/pitchspark
title: PitchSpark: Pre-Seed & Seed Deal Flow
description: Search scored pre-seed & seed startups that are actively raising, by sector, stage or query.

tools.name: pitchspark_get_pitch_v1
tools.description: Read the full public pitch of one early-stage startup from a PitchSpark search, by pitch_id: problem and solution, traction, market size, business model, competitors, moat, highlights, team size, HQ region, the ask, green flags and pitchspark_score (PitchSpark's AI pitch score, 0-100; null when the pitch has not been scored). Use it to screen a pre-seed or seed deal in depth before requesting an intro. This is the older single-purpose version: prefer pitchspark_get_pitch_v2, which returns this same pitch plus its score and anonymised decisions in one call. Founder claims are self-reported; financials, decks and founder contact details are not included.

pitch_id.description: The "id" of a search result, copied exactly.

tools.name: pitchspark_get_health_v1
tools.description: Check that PitchSpark's pre-seed and seed deal-flow search is up before running a batch of startup searches. Returns {"status":"ok","version":"2.0.0"} and no pitch data. No key needed; uses none of the daily pitch allowance.

tools.name: pitchspark_submit_pitch_v1
tools.description: For founders raising a pre-seed or seed round: create a draft pitch on your own PitchSpark account from five facts (company name, sector, stage, raise amount in USD, a one-paragraph problem statement). The draft is not listed, searchable or scored until the founder completes it and submits it for review in Pitch Studio at the returned edit_url. Needs a founder submit token (pss_..., from PitchSpark Settings). Where OAuth is enabled, a token with the pitches:submit scope also works. Returns pitch_id, status "draft", company_name and edit_url.

company_name.description: The startup's name, one line, e.g. "Acme Robotics".

sector.description: Primary sector, e.g. "fintech". Keys: fintech, healthtech, saas, marketplace, ai_ml, consumer, enterprise, climate, edtech, crypto, biotech, hardware, gaming, real_estate, food_beverage, fashion, travel, sports, media, femtech, cybersecurity, dev_tools, ecommerce, logistics, mobility, hr_tech, legal_tech, insurtech, proptech, agtech, energy, robotics, govtech, hospitality, other.

stage.description: Stage of the round being raised, e.g. "seed".

raise_amount_usd.description: Amount being raised in US dollars, e.g. 1500000.

problem_statement.description: One paragraph (40 to 1200 characters) on the problem and who has it. Its first sentence becomes the tagline.

tools.name: pitchspark_request_intro_v1
tools.description: For investors who found a startup to invest in: ask the founders of one PitchSpark pitch (by pitch_id) to connect, with a short message, through PitchSpark's in-app contact flow. Founders reply inside PitchSpark; their contact details are never returned. Returns status (requested, already_requested or quota_exhausted), intro_id and next_steps. Needs a PitchSpark API key (psk_...) from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation), or where OAuth is enabled a token for one with the intros:write scope. PitchSpark does not verify investors or founders, does not recommend investments and takes no part in any resulting deal.

pitch_id.description: The "id" of a search or details result, copied exactly.

message.description: The investor's note to the founders: who they are and why they are interested. Up to 1000 characters are kept; emails, phone numbers, links and @handles are removed.

tools.name: pitchspark_watch_pitch_v1
tools.description: For investors building a deal-flow shortlist: save one startup pitch (by pitch_id) to your PitchSpark saved pitches, to come back to on pitchspark.io. The founders are not contacted; the save counts as interest in their pitch statistics, where investors are numbered and never named. Saving again changes nothing. Returns status (watching, already_watching or limit_reached), pitch_id and next_steps. Needs a PitchSpark API key (psk_...) from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation), or where OAuth is enabled a token for one with the watchlist:write scope.

pitch_id.description: The "id" of a search or details result, copied exactly.

tools.name: pitchspark_get_pitch_v2
tools.description: Read one startup pitch by id and choose what comes back with "sections": "pitch" (the full public pitch, the same object as pitchspark_get_pitch_v1), "score" (score and roast, as pitchspark_get_score_v1), "decisions" (anonymised decision aggregates by signed-in users, as pitchspark_get_decision_summary_v1). Default: all three. Use when: an investor wants the whole picture of one shortlisted pitch in one call. Prefer the single-purpose tools when you only need one part. Link the pitch with its spark_card_url; the investor sign-up link a reply may carry in _meta (it returns a new investor to this pitch after sign-up) is not a pitch link. Do not use for: searching (pitchspark_search_pitches_v3), founder contact details, financials, decks or data rooms (never returned), investment advice. Anonymous callers can use it under the daily allowance; dimension scores and analyses need an API key, and the decisions section an investor API key. Decision data from signed-in PitchSpark users needs a PitchSpark API key from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation): without one every decision block is available false with reason key_required. It is anonymised: counts of distinct people only, as bands ("5-9", "10-24", "25-49", "50+"), never who; shares and rates to the nearest 0.05; the pitch's founders, team and PitchSpark staff are never counted; guest and anonymous viewers are never counted; every block is withheld (reason below_min_k) when fewer than 5 distinct people are behind it, and a split (positive vs pass, rating bands) is withheld when any part of it would be under 5; no investor comment text is ever returned. Who is counted: ratings, reading time, sections and score views count ANY signed-in non-owner user (the writers check no account type), and likes, passes and pass reasons count signed-in users who swiped or gave pass feedback (also not restricted to investor accounts); only the caller of this tool must hold an investor key. Some fields are withheld pending a review (reason hidden_pending_review, or absent from a list): the team-related pass reasons and the pass rate (the likes-vs-passes thumbs block, the search card signal, investors_considered and the card-dwell figures). Treat a withheld field as no signal. An id that does not exist, a pitch that is not public and a pitch whose founders opted out of AI agents all answer NOT_FOUND. Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view.

id.description: The pitch id from a search result ("id").

tools.name: pitchspark_get_score_v1
tools.description: Get PitchSpark's AI pitch score for one pitch: the composite (0-100), the six dimensions (market, problem, traction, moat, financials, team, each 0-100 with the model's analysis) and the Roast Room commentary when the pitch was roasted. Older single-purpose tool: prefer pitchspark_get_pitch_v2 with sections ["score"], the newer combined tool, which returns this same score object and can add the pitch and decisions in the same call. Call this one only for a client already built on it. Use when: an investor asks how PitchSpark rates a pitch, or where it is strong and weak, and pitchspark_get_pitch_v2 is not available to the client. Do not use for: scoring your own text (pitchspark_roast_text_v1, when enabled), what signed-in users decided (pitchspark_get_decision_summary_v1), investment advice. Limits of the data: the score is returned at any value; pitchspark_score is null only when the pitch has not been scored (dimensions_withheld "not_scored"). Dimensions and analyses need an API key (dimensions_withheld "key_required" without one). Roast text is filtered for personal attacks and contact details. Same access as pitchspark_get_pitch_v1: anonymous callers allowed under the daily allowance. Returns {"score":{pitch_id, company_name, pitchspark_score, scale, public_min, dimensions, dimensions_withheld, scoring_version, scored_at, roast}, "attribution"}. Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view.

id.description: The pitch id from a search result ("id").

tools.name: pitchspark_get_decision_summary_v1
tools.description: Summarise how signed-in PitchSpark users (not only investors) responded to one pitch: positive (likes and superlikes) vs passes (the thumbs block, currently withheld pending review: reason hidden_pending_review), the rating distribution and average (out of 10, to the nearest 0.5), the top pass reasons and "why we passed" themes (the team-related reasons and the team theme are withheld pending review and never listed; shares are over the listed reasons), time spent, and which pitch sections and score dimensions users read. Older single-purpose tool: prefer pitchspark_get_pitch_v2 with sections ["decisions"], the newer combined tool, which returns this same summary and can add the pitch and score in the same call. Call this one only for a client already built on it. Use when: an investor (or a founder's assistant) wants the crowd signal behind a pitch before deciding, and pitchspark_get_pitch_v2 is not available to the client. Do not use for: who passed or liked (never returned), investor comments (never returned), the AI score (pitchspark_get_score_v1). Decision data from signed-in PitchSpark users needs a PitchSpark API key from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation): without one every decision block is available false with reason key_required. It is anonymised: counts of distinct people only, as bands ("5-9", "10-24", "25-49", "50+"), never who; shares and rates to the nearest 0.05; the pitch's founders, team and PitchSpark staff are never counted; guest and anonymous viewers are never counted; every block is withheld (reason below_min_k) when fewer than 5 distinct people are behind it, and a split (positive vs pass, rating bands) is withheld when any part of it would be under 5; no investor comment text is ever returned. Who is counted: ratings, reading time, sections and score views count ANY signed-in non-owner user (the writers check no account type), and likes, passes and pass reasons count signed-in users who swiped or gave pass feedback (also not restricted to investor accounts); only the caller of this tool must hold an investor key. Some fields are withheld pending a review (reason hidden_pending_review, or absent from a list): the team-related pass reasons and the pass rate (the likes-vs-passes thumbs block, the search card signal, investors_considered and the card-dwell figures). Treat a withheld field as no signal. Sources: signed-in users' swipe decisions (likes, passes, pass reasons, card dwell), structured pass feedback (never comment text), ratings, time on the pitch page and per-section dwell, and score-dimension views. A block with no source data is available false, reason no_data. Returns {"pitch_id","company_name","decisions":{min_k, investors_considered, truncated, thumbs, rating, pass_reasons, pass_themes, time_spent, sections, score_dimension_interest},"attribution"}. Without an investor API key the call still answers (and counts against the allowance like pitchspark_get_pitch_v1), but every block is withheld. Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view.

id.description: The pitch id from a search result ("id").

tools.name: pitchspark_compare_pitches_v1
tools.description: Compare 2 to 4 pitches side by side: ask, stage, sector, HQ region, traction note, green flags, public score, dimension scores (keyed callers) and compact decision aggregates (likes vs passes, average rating, top pass reasons; investor API keys only, else reason key_required; each withheld below 5 distinct signed-in users, counts as bands; the likes-vs-passes block may be withheld with reason hidden_pending_review, and the team-related pass reasons are withheld pending review). Use when: an investor is choosing between shortlisted pitches. Do not use for: more than 4 pitches (run pitchspark_search_pitches_v3 sorted by score instead), full pitch text (pitchspark_get_pitch_v2). All ids must be distinct and resolvable: any id that is missing, not public or opted out answers NOT_FOUND for the whole call, and nothing is counted. The whole comparison is delivered or nothing is (a spent allowance answers RATE_LIMITED). Returns {"pitches":[...in the order given], "attribution"}. Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view.

items.description: The pitch id from a search result ("id").

tools.name: pitchspark_thesis_fit_v1
tools.description: Rank PitchSpark pitches by how well they fit an investment thesis: either thesis text you pass, or the investor's saved thesis and preferences on PitchSpark (use_saved_thesis). Each result has a fit_score (0-100) and a rationale listing exactly which criteria matched. Use when: an investor asks "what fits my thesis". Prefer pitchspark_search_pitches_v3 for explicit filters. Do not use for: investment advice; the fit is a rule-based match, not a judgement. How it works (rule_based_v1, no model call): the thesis is read for sectors, stages, HQ regions and keywords (the same rules as search); a pitch earns points for each criterion it meets (sector 35, stage 25, region 10, keywords up to 30), scaled to the criteria the thesis names. Pitches that meet none are left out. Requires a PitchSpark API key (psk_...). The thesis text is never logged or stored. Returns {"pitches":[{card, fit_score, rationale}], "thesis", "method", "attribution"}. Up to 10 results (25 on a paid key). Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view.

thesis_text.description: The thesis in plain English, 20 to 2000 characters. Not with use_saved_thesis.

use_saved_thesis.description: true: use the thesis and sector / stage / geography preferences saved on the key owner's PitchSpark profile. Not with thesis_text.

limit.description: How many ranked pitches to return, 1 up to the caller's tier ceiling (10 on a free or anonymous call, 25 on a paid key). A higher value is reduced to the ceiling.

tools.name: pitchspark_list_watchlist_v1
tools.description: List the pitches the investor has saved on PitchSpark (in the app or with pitchspark_watch_pitch_v1), newest first: id, company name, stage, sector, when saved and the link. Use when: the investor asks what is on their watchlist or saved pitches. Do not use for: saving (pitchspark_watch_pitch_v1), searching. Requires a PitchSpark API key from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation). Pitches that are no longer public or whose founders opted out of AI agents are left out and counted in unavailable_count. Up to 50 items. Uses none of the daily pitch allowance. Read-only. Calls are logged.

limit.description: How many saved pitches to return, newest first, 1 to 50.

tools.name: pitchspark_pipeline_stage_v1
tools.description: Read the investor's own PitchSpark deal pipeline: for each pitch, its stage (sparked, deck_requested, in_conversation, due_diligence, invested), when it last moved and whether it is archived. Optionally one pitch_id. Use when: the investor asks where a deal stands. Do not use for: moving a deal (not available through this server; use PitchSpark), other investors' pipelines (never). Requires a PitchSpark API key from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation). Only the key owner's own rows are read. Notes and investment amounts are never returned (has_notes says whether there are notes). Pitches no longer public or opted out are left out (unavailable_count). Up to 50 items. Read-only; uses none of the daily pitch allowance.

pitch_id.description: Optional: read the pipeline stage of this one pitch only (the "id" of a search result, copied exactly). Leave out to list every pipeline row.

include_archived.description: true: also list deals the investor archived (passed or removed). false (default): active deals only.

tools.name: pitchspark_save_search_v1
tools.description: Save a search (the query and filters of pitchspark_search_pitches_v3) under the caller's API key, to list and re-run later with pitchspark_list_saved_searches_v1. Use when: the investor asks to save or remember a search. Do not use for: alerts (not delivered yet: saving does not send anything), running the search (pitchspark_search_pitches_v3). Requires a PitchSpark API key with the searches:write scope (keys without a scope list hold it). Idempotent: the same normalised query and filters under the same key returns the existing saved search (status "already_saved") and writes nothing new. At most 20 saved searches per key (status "limit_reached"); 50 saves per key per UTC day (RATE_LIMITED). Do not put personal data (names, emails, phone numbers, anything about a person) in "name" or "query": they are stored for up to 180 days. Emails and phone numbers that do appear are stored as [redacted]. Saved searches are deleted 180 days after they were last saved, and with the account. Returns {"status","saved_search","max_per_key","next_steps"}.

name.description: A short label, e.g. "Seed fintech in Europe".

query.description: Optional: what the investor is looking for, in plain language, 1 to 500 characters. Ranked by meaning when semantic ranking is available, by keyword + synonym otherwise (search_mode says which). A query asking for the newest pitches ("most recent", "newest", "latest") is ordered as sort recency. Leave it out to browse the filtered pitches by score and recency.

sector.description: Sector key or list of up to 10 (primary or additional sector). Keys: fintech, healthtech, saas, marketplace, ai_ml, consumer, enterprise, climate, edtech, crypto, biotech, hardware, gaming, real_estate, food_beverage, fashion, travel, sports, media, femtech, cybersecurity, dev_tools, ecommerce, logistics, mobility, hr_tech, legal_tech, insurtech, proptech, agtech, energy, robotics, govtech, hospitality, other.

stage.description: Funding stage or list. "early" means pre_seed, seed and series_a.

location.description: HQ region key or list: us, canada, latam, uk, europe, mea, apac, global_remote.

min_raise_usd.description: Raise at least this many US dollars (disclosed asks only).

max_raise_usd.description: Raise at most this many US dollars (disclosed asks only).

green_flags.description: Traction signal: at least one of these founder-chosen green flags (e.g. "Profitable", "Signed LOI").

has_traction.description: Traction signal: true = only pitches with a public traction note.

min_score.description: PitchSpark score at least this, 0 to 100 (pitches without a score are left out).

created_within_days.description: Recency: listed on PitchSpark within this many days.

updated_within_days.description: Recency: pitch updated within this many days.

sort.description: relevance (default: by meaning or keyword with a query, by a score and recency blend without one), score (public score, highest first), recency (newest submitted first: the date the pitch was submitted to PitchSpark, each card's created_at; use it for "most recent", "newest" or "latest" pitches, no query needed), most_viewed_by_investors (Pitch.views_count, all viewers), recently_updated (last edited first, updated_at). Any sort but relevance orders by that key and never ranks by meaning.

include_seen.description: false (default): pitches this caller (API key, OAuth account, MCP session or anon id) was shown in the last 7 days are left out. true: neither leaves them out nor records this reply.

tools.name: pitchspark_list_saved_searches_v1
tools.description: List the searches saved with pitchspark_save_search_v1 under the caller's API key, newest first, each with the exact arguments to re-run it ("rerun": tool pitchspark_search_pitches_v3 and its arguments). Use when: the investor asks for their saved searches. Do not use for: running them (pass rerun.arguments to pitchspark_search_pitches_v3). Requires a PitchSpark API key (psk_...). Searches are per key, not per account. Read-only; uses none of the daily pitch allowance.

tools.name: pitchspark_unwatch_pitch_v1
tools.description: Remove one startup pitch (by pitch_id) from the investor's PitchSpark saved pitches, the list that pitchspark_watch_pitch_v1 adds to and pitchspark_list_watchlist_v1 reads. Use when: the investor asks to unsave, unwatch or drop a pitch from their saved pitches. Do not use for: finding startups (pitchspark_search_pitches_v3), saving a pitch (pitchspark_watch_pitch_v1), passing on a deal or moving it in the pipeline (done on pitchspark.io), contacting founders. Only the key owner's own saved row is removed and the founders are not told. A pitch that is also in the investor's active deal pipeline stays saved (status "in_pipeline"): manage it on pitchspark.io. Removing a pitch that is not saved changes nothing (status "not_watching"). Requires a PitchSpark API key (psk_...) from an investor account (self-declared; PitchSpark does not verify accreditation), or where OAuth is enabled a token for one with the watchlist:write scope. Uses none of the daily pitch allowance. Returns {"status" (removed, not_watching or in_pipeline), "pitch_id", "next_steps"}.

pitch_id.description: The "id" of a search, details or watchlist result, copied exactly.

tools.name: pitchspark_delete_saved_search_v1
tools.description: Delete one search saved with pitchspark_save_search_v1 under the caller's API key, by its saved_search_id (the "id" from pitchspark_save_search_v1 or pitchspark_list_saved_searches_v1). Use when: the investor asks to delete, remove or forget a saved search. Do not use for: finding startups (pitchspark_search_pitches_v3), listing saved searches (pitchspark_list_saved_searches_v1), removing saved pitches (pitchspark_unwatch_pitch_v1). Only a search saved under the same API key can be deleted; the deletion cannot be undone, but the search can be saved again. An id that is not found changes nothing (status "not_found"). Requires a PitchSpark API key with the searches:write scope (keys without a scope list hold it). Uses none of the daily pitch allowance. Returns {"status" (deleted or not_found), "saved_search_id", "next_steps"}.

saved_search_id.description: The "id" of a saved search, copied exactly from pitchspark_save_search_v1 or pitchspark_list_saved_searches_v1.

tools.name: pitchspark_search_pitches_v3
tools.description: Search the startup pitches listed on PitchSpark (pre-seed and seed rounds that founders list as raising; later rounds are listed too) and return lightweight cards with their pitch ids. The other PitchSpark pitch tools (pitchspark_get_pitch_v2, pitchspark_get_score_v1, pitchspark_get_decision_summary_v1, pitchspark_compare_pitches_v1) take a pitch id from this tool's results. This is PitchSpark's one search tool. With a query and semantic ranking available, it matches on meaning as well as words (e.g. "software that helps independent clinics get paid faster" can match revenue-cycle and payments pitches that never say "get paid"). Use when: the user asks to find, browse or filter startups on PitchSpark, by a description in their own words (a problem, a customer, a business model), by filters, sorted by score, recency, investor views or updates, or with no query. Do not use for: reading one pitch in depth (pitchspark_get_pitch_v2), ranking against a long written thesis (pitchspark_thesis_fit_v1), checking that the server is up (pitchspark_get_health_v1), saving or removing saved pitches or searches, founder contact details, decks or data rooms (never returned), investment advice. The filters (sector, stage incl. "early", HQ region, raise range, minimum public score, traction, green flags, listed or updated within N days) narrow the list first; the query then ranks what is left. Only the sector argument filters by sector, and a list of sectors means any of them (OR). Sectors named in the query only boost the ranking, and several named together combine with AND ("climate hardware" ranks pitches filed under both highest); "interpretation.sectors_applied" marks each as filter or boost. For the most recent, newest or latest pitches pass sort "recency" with limit N and no query: newest submitted to PitchSpark first (created_at on each card), and include_seen true so pitches already shown are not skipped; a query that asks for the newest is ordered the same way. Ranking uses embeddings when they are available (similarity blended with the public score and recency) and falls back to keyword + synonym ranking when they are not. Without a query or sort the filtered pitches are browsed by a public score and recency blend (not newest first); a sort other than relevance orders by that key. Every reply states which in "search_mode" (semantic, mixed, keyword_fallback, browse or sorted) with "fallback_reason". Pitches this caller was shown in the last 7 days are left out unless include_seen is true. Returns lightweight cards, "page" (cursor or offset paging) and "coverage". Email addresses and phone numbers are removed from the query before it is used. Link each pitch with its own spark_card_url: the investor sign-up link a reply may carry in _meta is not a pitch link. Each pitch this tool returns counts 1 against the daily pitch allowance (the one allowance every pitch tool shares), or 0 when the same API key (without a key, the same connection) already got that pitch today. Calls are logged, and each pitch returned is counted as a view. Errors are JSON {"error":{"code","message","category","retryable"}}: INVALID_ARGUMENT, UNAUTHORIZED, RATE_LIMITED, INTERNAL.

query.description: Optional: what the investor is looking for, in plain language, 1 to 500 characters. Ranked by meaning when semantic ranking is available, by keyword + synonym otherwise (search_mode says which). A query asking for the newest pitches ("most recent", "newest", "latest") is ordered as sort recency. Leave it out to browse the filtered pitches by score and recency.

sector.description: Sector key or list of up to 10 (primary or additional sector). Keys: fintech, healthtech, saas, marketplace, ai_ml, consumer, enterprise, climate, edtech, crypto, biotech, hardware, gaming, real_estate, food_beverage, fashion, travel, sports, media, femtech, cybersecurity, dev_tools, ecommerce, logistics, mobility, hr_tech, legal_tech, insurtech, proptech, agtech, energy, robotics, govtech, hospitality, other.

stage.description: Funding stage or list. "early" means pre_seed, seed and series_a.

location.description: HQ region key or list: us, canada, latam, uk, europe, mea, apac, global_remote.

min_raise_usd.description: Raise at least this many US dollars (disclosed asks only).

max_raise_usd.description: Raise at most this many US dollars (disclosed asks only).

green_flags.description: Traction signal: at least one of these founder-chosen green flags (e.g. "Profitable", "Signed LOI").

has_traction.description: Traction signal: true = only pitches with a public traction note.

min_score.description: PitchSpark score at least this, 0 to 100 (pitches without a score are left out).

created_within_days.description: Recency: listed on PitchSpark within this many days.

updated_within_days.description: Recency: pitch updated within this many days.

sort.description: relevance (default: by meaning or keyword with a query, by a score and recency blend without one), score (public score, highest first), recency (newest submitted first: the date the pitch was submitted to PitchSpark, each card's created_at; use it for "most recent", "newest" or "latest" pitches, no query needed), most_viewed_by_investors (Pitch.views_count, all viewers), recently_updated (last edited first, updated_at). Any sort but relevance orders by that key and never ranks by meaning.
